source_read: PMC HTML full text, PMC1976310 (abstract, Background, Methods, Results, Table 1 with footnotes, Discussion, Conclusion), read in my own browser tab; Table 1 arithmetic recomputed

claims.overstatement: Minor wording points, numbers all correct. (1) '21 outside its category for people with a known history of problem drug use': np-SAD classed 21 as 'not a drug abuser/dependent' and a further 11 as 'unknown', so 32 were outside the drug abuser/dependent category; 'classed 21 as not drug-dependent (11 unknown)' is exact. (2) The three counts overlap and are not additive (2 of the 21 and 4 of the 11 'unknown' were among the 25 non-toxicity deaths; overlap with the 15 non-residents is not reported). (3) The paper reports residence (Table 1) without comment; it does not attribute the 15 non-residents to the wider definition, so listing them under 'wider local definitions add other deaths' is the claim's inference (a place-of-death versus residence difference), not the authors'.
claims.note: 25 and 15 are editors' arithmetic from Table 1 totals (70 - 45 toxicity deaths; 70 - 55 Liverpool residents); both recomputed and correct. '70 deaths ... deaths in 2004 and inquests in January to June 2005' matches the Methods (57 + 28 with 15 double counts removed). 'Coroner-fed' is consistent with the paper (np-SAD criteria rest on the coroner's report; data retrieved from coroner records). The paper also gives the contrast that makes the point: national and European figures use a compact definition, the local performance figures the wider np-SAD one.

anchors.extracted: UK Drug Strategy (national) definition: underlying cause poisoning, drug abuse or drug dependence with a substance controlled under the Misuse of Drugs Act 1971 involved (16,088 deaths 1993-2004). Local figures used to performance-monitor Drug (and Alcohol) Action Teams come from np-SAD with a wider definition: all psychoactive substances, controlled or not; 'relevant deaths' where substances were implicated (with or without post-mortem), where there is a history of drug abuse, or where controlled drugs were present at post-mortem.

np-SAD reported 57 Liverpool deaths occurring in 2004 (annual report) and 28 drug-related-death inquests completed in Liverpool in January-June 2005 (surveillance report); double counts removed, 70 deaths. Data from Liverpool DAAT and coroner records. np-SAD classes deaths as drug abuser/dependent (known history of drug abuse plus one of four criteria: coroner reports known illicit drug use; prescribed substitute medication; non-prescribed illicit drug at post-mortem; other information on the coroner's report), non-drug abuser/dependent (none met) or unknown (information unavailable).

anchors.locator: Table 1 (rows n, Resident in Liverpool, Death from drug(s) toxicity; footnote 4)
anchors.extracted: n = 70: drug abuser/dependent 38, not a drug abuser/dependent 21, unknown 11. Resident in Liverpool 55 (78.6%), so 15 non-residents (editors' arithmetic; 11, 3 and 1 by group). Death from drug(s) toxicity 45 (64.3%; includes toxicity from prescribed drugs), so 25 not from drug toxicity (editors' arithmetic; 19, 2 and 4 by group: 19/38 50.0%, 19/21 90.5%, 7/11 63.6% toxicity deaths).

Half the deaths were classed by np-SAD as drug abusers; the non-drug-abuser deaths varied widely (example: a person over 90 with coronary heart disease who died of myocardial insufficiency with contributory carbamazepine toxicity); non-drug abusers were older (median 53.59 vs 38.23 years; z = 3.942, P < 0.001) and none had recent drug-treatment or criminal-justice contact; most of their toxicity deaths involved anti-depressants, anti-psychotics and opioid analgesics.

England and Wales and European figures use a similar compact definition, while the wider np-SAD definition used for local performance monitoring lets large numbers of people who do not appear to be drug abusers into the figures, mostly deaths from psychoactive medicines not necessarily controlled under the 1971 Act.

claims.note: Correctly framed as the authors' argument: the infection figures behind it (16% of deaths among treatment clients from infections; about half of people who inject drugs in the UK infected with hepatitis C; an estimated 4% progressing to severe cirrhosis) are cited from other studies, not measured in this paper. 'UK and European definitions of the time' = np-SAD, England and Wales and European definitions as named in the paper. Not cited by the claim but bearing on its first sentence (counts also include deaths a fuller review would not call drug deaths) and on the register-composition sentence: the same np-SAD register's 70 Liverpool deaths included 25 not from drug toxicity and 21 of people classed as not drug-dependent (Table 1).

anchors.extracted: The authors state that the np-SAD, England and Wales and European definitions exclude deaths from bacterial and viral infections, often transmitted through injecting, although these are a sizeable share of drug-related mortality; cited from other studies: 16% of deaths of drug-treatment clients in North West England were due to infections; nearly half of UK people who inject drugs have hepatitis C; an estimated 4% progress to severe cirrhosis, deaths the definitions exclude. They propose adding deaths from blood-borne factors to the international definition.

Deaths known to be associated with drug use, such as those from chronic hepatitis C infection, are excluded from local, national and European definitions; with current definitions the true burden of drug-related mortality in the UK and Europe remains unknown.

anchors.locator: Table 1 (row Death from drug(s) toxicity) and Discussion, 1st paragraph
anchors.extracted: Inclusion direction: of 70 deaths the np-SAD register counted for Liverpool, 45 were from drug toxicity (25 not, editors' arithmetic) and 21 were of people classed as not drug abusers/dependent; the authors argue the wide definition includes many deaths outside the focus of drug services.
